_status: The firm identity values here (name, attorney, bar number, address, phone, e-mail, letterhead, roster) are the sample firm's, shipped so a copy nothing was configured on can fill a demonstration case: Settings, Main office overrides each of them, and for a firm that has configured the product (the installer saved its name) they reach no form and no letter until it has saved its own details (src/settings.py shipped). Companion forms filed with the I-485: Form G-28 (the attorney's notice of appearance) and Form I-765 (work permit). Field names are the forms' own (short form; src/fill/companion.py finds the full name, and fills every copy of a name, e.g. the name pre-printed again on the last page). Templates downloaded from uscis.gov on 2026-10-01: G-28 edition 09/17/18, I-765 edition 08/21/25. The 'constants' are firm choices for SIJS filings and need the attorney's approval before volume use (docs/decisions.md 2026-10-01). Left blank on purpose, for the attorney: the G-28 licensing authority (until the firm adds firm.licensing_authority), the G-28 'subject to any order' statement and notice options, and the I-765 'previously filed' and language statements. Form I-360 (Special Immigrant Juvenile) and its own G-28 added 2026-10-01: Part 2 'C', 'no other petitions' and 'no I-485 attached' are the constants for an I-360 filed alone; a concurrent filing changes them (attorney). Family-based filing (spouse of a U.S. citizen first) added 2026-10-01: Forms I-130 (04/01/24), I-130A (04/01/24), I-864 (08/24/26) and the petitioner's own G-28; petitioner.* facts are the U.S. citizen or permanent resident relative's.

Part 8, item 1 (the client reads English, or an interpreter read the form to them) and Part 9 for the interpreter.
Part 11 for any Yes answer in Part 7 (each explained with places and dates), and for earlier TPS applications.

i765_tps.title: Form I-765, Application for Employment Authorization (TPS, category (a)(12) or (c)(19))
i765_tps._note: The work permit's own map (forms.ead) on the same template, edition 08/21/25, with its 'ead.' answers renamed 'tps_ead.' so a TPS filing never takes an earlier work permit filing's answers (src/fill/companion.py _borrow_map). Category (a)(12) (TPS granted) or (c)(19) (a pending applicant found prima facie eligible) in Part 2, 27 (the I-765 page's list of categories).
attorney_completes: Part 3, item 1: the client reads English, or an interpreter read the form to them (and the language), and Part 4 for the interpreter.
Part 2, items 2-4: other names used, if any.
Write the name, date of birth and mailing address exactly as on the I-821.

g28_tps.title: Form G-28, Notice of Entry of Appearance as Attorney (for the I-821 and I-765)
g28_tps._note: The G-28 for the I-765 (forms.g28_ead), listing the I-821 and the I-765.
attorney_completes: Part 2, item 1.a: the licensing authority (the state's highest court), or set the bar admission on the Settings page (The firm and the attorney).
Part 2, item 1.c: whether the attorney is or is not subject to any order restricting their practice.
Part 4, items 2.a-2.c: how the client wants USCIS notices and secure documents sent.

i131_parole.title: Form I-131, Application for Travel Documents, Parole Documents, and Arrival/Departure Records (initial parole for someone outside the U.S.)
i131_parole._note: Edition 01/20/25 (the same template as forms.i131; uscis.gov/i-131, updated 08/14/2026, read 2026-10-02). Part 1, item 7: 'initial parole document ... for myself and I am outside the United States, or ... on behalf of someone else who is outside the United States ... but not under a specific parole program or process': the page-3 box P3[0].CB_AppType[5] (/23). Part 2, items 1-15 are about the person who files (the client); items 16-27 about the person the parole is for, only when someone else files (I-131 Instructions, Part 2). When the client files for themself, items 16-27 stay blank and Parts 3 and 4 are the client's own. Part 4's items 2.a and 3.a are answered; the form then says 'SKIP to Part 8' (items 4-7 and Parts 5-7 are skipped for parole from outside the U.S.). Part 2, item 13 of the printed form's refugee question is Part 1, item 13. The same map serves each person the parole is for: src/parole.py puts that person's answers under the 'parole.them.' (items 16-27) and 'parole.bio.' (Parts 3 and 4) keys (src/packet.py: one form per person).
attorney_completes: Part 2, items 2 and 17: other names used, if any.
Part 11 if an interpreter was used.
Part 8, item 1: the explanation is the short version; the detailed statement and the evidence go with it (I-131 Instructions, Part 8).
Part 1, item 13 (refugee status), unless the case answers it, and Part 4, items 2.b-2.c and 3.b-3.c when 2.a or 3.a is Yes, if not answered.
Part 4, items 4-9 and Parts 5-7 are skipped for parole from outside the U.S.: the form says to skip to Part 8 after item 3.c.

i134.title: Form I-134, Declaration of Financial Support
i134._note: Edition 01/20/25 (uscis.gov/i-134, updated 06/03/2026; downloaded 2026-10-02). One I-134 for each beneficiary, by each supporter ('You must file a separate Form I-134 for each beneficiary': the page): src/parole.py fills it for each person the parole is for and for one supporter. Many boxes repeat their name on the supporter's pages and the beneficiary's (the mailing address, the date of birth, the place of birth, the contact boxes): mapped by their parent names (src/fill/companion.py takes a name with up to two parents). The supporter signs Part 5 on page 8 (a beneficiary who supports themself signs Part 4 on page 6). The Part 4 and Part 5 statement boxes (reads English, an interpreter, a preparer) are left to the attorney. The beneficiary's anticipated period of stay is Part 3, item 12.

supporter: Part 5, item 6 (page 8), the supporter's signature; the boxes before the interpreter's

attorney_completes: Part 2, item 2 and Part 3, item 2: other names used, if any.
Part 2, item 15: the table of the supporter's dependents (each with a date of birth, relationship and A-Number or receipt number).
Part 5, items 1-2 (the supporter reads English, or an interpreter read it to them; a preparer helped) and Part 6 for an interpreter.
A supporter who is the beneficiary and supports themself signs Part 4, item 6 (page 6) instead of Part 5.
Part 8 for any answer that needs more room (more than three assets, for one).
